topics.label: Introduction to cancer causation and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, context of the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiological factors and epidemiological patterns in cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental balance between intrinsic genetic processes, environmental exposures, and epidemiological patterns that determine cancer risk.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical and physical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to cause DNA adducts, transversions, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages influence cancer development alongside mutational events.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by summarising the challenges of determining carcinogenicity and discussing daily risk-benefit decisions regarding exposure.
